reason: A likeness to a rose that means different things in each use: a scent of the flower, or prickles like those of Rosa. It names no quality on its own.
A comparison stated without its second term (enlarged compared with the ovary, the rest of the achene, the other cells). 'Scarcely' leaves it between enlarged and not enlarged.
A saucer is already shallow, so 'shallowly' adds nothing that needs a term. The value is saucer-shaped.
A smudge is an irregular blot of another colour: PATO_0000329 blotchy (synonym blotched). Its colour (black, yellow) is a separate colour value.
PATO_0001609 sparse is defined as scattered, spread irregularly and at a distance from each other, which is the phrase itself. It applies to the hairs or glands that are scattered.

It means stamens at different heights in one use and flowers or fruits spaced along an axis ('échelonnés') in another. That is too unclear for a term, and the stamen sense is a relation between members of a set.
A spelling variant of thyrse-like, which was added in the previous review.

target: new: two values of one bearer (villous FLOPO:0991051 and ciliated PATO_0001408)
reason: This is not a range between two values. The margin or sepal is fringed (ciliolate, minutely ciliate) with long soft hairs (villous), so both values hold together, as decided for 'obliquely ovate'.
A habitat (the elevation zone above the tree line), not a quality of the plant's form. Unlike epiphytic or aquatic, it says nothing about how the plant is placed.
A generic part that needs the organ it belongs to, as with 'claw' and 'beak'. PO has only leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106), which does not fit petals, stipules or wings.
Bifarious means arranged in two opposite rows, which is PATO_0001952 distichous. In 'bifariously pubescent' it applies to the hairs, which run in two lines down the stem.
A bulky taproot, rhizome or crown is large and massive: PATO_0000586 increased size, as decided for 'enlarged'.
Apiculate (ending abruptly in a short point) with a hardened, callose tip is the abrupt, short, stiff point of mucronate. PATO has 'apiculate' only as a synonym of the attribute sharpness.
Carpellate flowers are female, as decided for 'pistillate'. 'Fruits 3-carpellés' is a count of carpels (docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md), so the rule is limited to flowers.
This is not a range between two values. The apex runs out into a tail ending in a stiff point, and both hold. Caudate is the more specific of the two, as decided for 'caudate-acuminate'.
A cigar is a long cylinder with blunt, slightly narrowed ends, as with mangrove hypocotyls and long fruits. Cylindrical is the nearest term; fusiform would wrongly say it is widest in the middle.

target: new: two values of one bearer (puberulous FLOPO:0991049 and ciliated PATO_0001408)
reason: The surface is minutely hairy and the margin fringed with hairs, so both values hold at once. This is not a range between them.
A hyphenated pair of two shapes is a range between clavate (PATO_0001883) and cylindrical (PATO_0001873), as decided for 'ovate-lanceolate'.
'Claw equal to limb' and 'onglet égalant les sépales' compare the length of one part with another. The claw is the part of the bearer that is compared.
A compound corymb is a corymb whose branches are themselves corymbs. Its shape is corymb-like, and how many times it branches is not a separate term.
Teeth in between rounded and saw-like: a range between scalloped (PATO_0001889, synonym crenate) and serrated (PATO_0001206).
A cymose panicle is a much-branched inflorescence whose last branches are cymes, so it is panicle-like. Thyrse-like would assume an indeterminate main axis, which floras do not always mean.
A count of cystoliths with the vague number 'numerous', as decided for 'few-flowered'. Cystolith has no PO class, so the bearer needs one before the count can be annotated.
A margin in between toothed and small-lobed: a range between dentated (PATO_0001205) and lobed (PATO_0001979, as for 'lobulate').

It means the auricles are absent, but the only PO auricle class is leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106), which is wrong for leaflets and stipules. A rule cannot work until there is a general auricle class.
A range between elliptic (PATO_0000947) and pandurate. Pandurate (fiddle-shaped) has no PATO or FLOPO term yet, so only the elliptic end can be annotated until it is added.
Fat branches, stems and mid-lobes are thick and stout: PATO_0000591 increased thickness (synonyms stout, thickened).
Fernlike leaves are finely cut into many segments like a fern frond: dissected is the nearest term. The likeness to a fern says nothing more than that.
A range between fan-shaped (PATO_0002219, as for 'flabellate') and obovate (PATO_0001936).
'Stipules gland-shaped' says the stipules are reduced to glands. That is a statement about what the part is, not a shape, and glands have no shape of their own to name.
